QXO reports Q3 results, on track for $50B annual revenue by end of decade says CEO
November 19, 2026 | 8:17 am CST
QXO reports Q3 results, on track for $50B annual revenue by end of decade says CEO

GREENWICH, Conn. — QXO, Inc. has reported financial results for the third quarter of 2026. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, basic and diluted loss per common share was $(0.17). Adjusted Diluted Earnings per Common Share, a non-GAAP financial measure, was $0.13.

Note: The following summary of financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, includes the legacy Kodiak Building Partners, Inc. (“Kodiak”) operational results from the date of acquisition on April 1, 2026, through September 30, 2026, and the legacy TopBuild Corp. (“TopBuild”) operational results from the date of the acquisition on July 1, 2026, through September 30, 2026. The summary of financial results for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, includes the legacy Beacon Roofing Supply, Inc. (“Beacon”) operational results from the date of acquisition on April 29, 2025, through September 30, 2025.

Brad Jacobs, chairman and chief executive officer of QXO, said, “Our organic daily revenue trends improved for the second consecutive quarter despite a soft construction market. Companywide pricing increased 2.2% year over year. We’re prioritizing higher-margin products; in Roofing and Waterproofing, complementary product sales grew 4.2%, and TRI-BUILT reached a record 10.6% of sales. Mechanical insulation distribution revenue grew 16%, supported by strong data center demand.”

Jacobs continued, “We have significant opportunities to grow by further integrating our businesses. We serve 194,000 customers across the legacy Beacon, Kodiak, and TopBuild businesses, but typically supply only a portion of what they need for a project. Our broader offering helps customers work with fewer suppliers, coordinate installation, and reduce construction costs. We’re also improving our purchasing terms and applying successful operating practices from individual businesses across QXO.

“Technology will help us serve customers better and operate more efficiently across our network. We’re connecting our sales, inventory, and warehouse systems so employees can access information more easily and spend less time entering data in multiple applications. Our people will be able to provide quotes faster, check inventory in real time, and respond to customers more quickly. AI will help salespeople identify opportunities to sell additional products and win back dormant accounts. Better delivery planning will improve service and reduce transportation costs.

“We’re on track to reach $4 billion in adjusted EBITDA by 2030 from the businesses we already own and $50 billion in annual revenue within the decade through organic growth and disciplined acquisitions.”

In addition, the Company’s Board of Directors has authorized a common share repurchase program of $500 million with no expiration date. The authorization to repurchase common shares will be used at management’s discretion, and the amount and timing of common share repurchases under the authorization will be subject to various factors. The program does not obligate the Company to repurchase any shares and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.
Net sales totaled $4.90 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2026, including $1.64 billion from TopBuild and $589 million from Kodiak.

For the third quarter of 2026, net loss was $123 million and Adjusted Net Income, a non-GAAP financial measure, was $229 million. Basic and diluted loss per common share was $(0.17) and Adjusted Diluted Earnings per Common Share, a non-GAAP financial measure, was $0.13.
Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP financial measure, was $557 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026.
